overview.overview:
South Carolina is expected to vote solidly Republican in 2028. It backed the Republican presidential candidate by about 11.7 points in 2020 and by about 17.9 points in 2024, and the central estimate is a Republican margin near ten points. The plausible range runs from a narrow Republican edge to a margin near twenty points. The state is considered very unlikely to decide the Electoral College.

The state's partisan baseline sits well to the right of the country as a whole, and the broader national environment shifts the outlook only modestly. No state-level polls are currently available. Nikki Haley, a South Carolina Republican, is a prominent figure in the state, but no separate adjustment is applied for a home-state candidate.
overview.watch: A significant national shift in opinion, or clear evidence in future polling of unusual movement among suburban and Black voters in South Carolina, would be the most likely thing to narrow the expected margin.
key_factors: A long-term Republican baseline that runs well ahead of the national average
A wider Republican margin in 2024 than in 2020
No public state polling, so the estimate rests mainly on past results and national conditions
